skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run hosted AI apps for images, video, language models, search, 3D assets, audio, and Twitter/X automation.
skill.summary: Run hosted AI apps from the inference.sh CLI.
skill.author: inference-sh-8

security_audit.summary: AI review confirms that many static findings are Markdown examples or passive documentation links, not hidden executable code. The audit confirms critical remote pipe-to-shell installation instructions, command-substitution install logic, filesystem writes into user configuration paths, hosted data transfer, and social platform automation risk. No prompt injection attempt or malicious credential exfiltration text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh in multiple install instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Make manual download, checksum verification, and signature verification the primary path. Avoid pipe-to-shell examples in marketplace-facing content.

remediation.issue: Manual install uses command substitution and shell pipelines based on a remote manifest.
remediation.suggestion: Provide platform-specific download URLs or a small verified installer command that avoids unquoted command substitution.

remediation.issue: The skill runs hosted apps and can send prompts, files, and task outputs to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit data-handling guidance and require users to approve sensitive prompts or files before running cloud apps.

remediation.issue: Twitter/X automation can publish or modify account activity.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for posts, direct messages, follows, likes, and reposts.

remediation.issue: API-key authentication is documented without storage and logging warnings near every usage path.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend secret managers, avoid shell history exposure, and never print INFSH_API_KEY in logs.

content.value_statement: Teams need one CLI workflow for many hosted AI models and media tools. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code discover apps, run tasks, and track results.
actual_capabilities: Documents installation, login, update, and API-key authentication for the inference.sh CLI.
Lists infsh commands for app discovery, search, filters, app details, and saved catalogs.
Provides examples for hosted image, video, LLM, audio, search, Twitter/X, and 3D apps.
Explains sample input creation, no-wait execution, task polling, JSON results, and saved outputs.
Links to inference.sh documentation for setup, app browsing, running apps, and deployment.
limitations: Requires the external infsh CLI and an inference.sh account.
Runs workloads on hosted services, so input data can leave the local machine.
Does not validate every third-party app, model, or generated result.
Twitter/X automation depends on account permissions and platform rules.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI Media Workflows
use_cases.description: Generate images, videos, audio, or 3D assets from prompts using documented inference.sh workflows.

use_cases.title: Run Model Experiments from a Terminal
use_cases.description: Search available apps, inspect schemas, create sample inputs, and compare hosted model outputs.

use_cases.title: Automate Cloud AI Tasks
use_cases.description: Use API-key authentication, no-wait runs, task polling, and saved results in repeatable scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Find an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-tools skill to find inference.sh apps for image generation. Show the safest steps I should follow.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Hosted Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inference.sh to run a hosted LLM app for this prompt: summarize this product brief in five bullets.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Media Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an inference.sh workflow for generating a short video from a text prompt. Include sample input creation and task tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CI Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI-safe inference.sh sequence that uses INFSH_API_KEY, starts a task, polls for completion, and saves results.

output_examples.input: Find a fast video generation app and run it from the CLI.
output: Suggested app: google/veo-3-1-fast for fast text-to-video generation.
Recommended steps: inspect the app, create a sample input, run it, then check the result.
Security note: avoid private customer data in prompts.
Use browser login for local interactive work.
Use INFSH_API_KEY for CI/CD or scripted workflows.
Store the key in the CI secret manager and avoid printing it in logs.

output_examples.input: Discover image apps and save the list.
output: Filter apps by image category or image-related keywords.
Save the catalog when you need repeatable comparison.
Inspect each app schema before sending production prompts.

best_practices: Review remote installer scripts or use manual installation before running them.
Store INFSH_API_KEY in a secret manager and keep it out of logs.
Inspect app schemas and privacy terms before sending sensitive prompts or files.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers to a shell in production environments.
Do not send secrets, private source code, or regulated data to hosted apps without approval.
Do not automate Twitter/X actions without account authorization and review controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant use the inference.sh CLI to discover apps, run hosted AI tasks, and track results.

faq.question: Does it require an external account?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow requires the infsh CLI and inference.sh authentication.

faq.question: Can it generate images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include FLUX image generation and Veo video generation through hosted apps.

faq.question: Can it call language models?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for Claude and other models through OpenRouter and inference.sh apps.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with confidential data?
faq.answer: Use caution. The workflow sends inputs to hosted services, so confidential data needs organizational approval first.

faq.question: Why does it need security review?
faq.answer: The documentation recommends a remote pipe-to-shell installer and authenticated cloud execution. Both require trust review before publication.
